quarterly_data.signal: Record quarter again: consolidated revenue reached NT$1.04 trillion with EPS of NT$7.43; revenue, gross profit, operating profit and quarterly EPS all set single-quarter records. Revenue grew 28.1% QoQ and 105.6% YoY. Gross profit was a record NT$52.08B (up 34.6% QoQ, 46.6% YoY) at a 5.02% gross margin (+24bp QoQ, -202bp YoY); operating profit NT$34.2B (+48.7% QoQ, +67.8% YoY) with the opex ratio at a record-low 1.72%; net profit a record NT$28.65B (+35.2% QoQ, +69.9% YoY). Trailing-12-month ROE broke above 40% for the first time. H1 revenue was NT$1.8458T, up 86.5% YoY, with H1 EPS of NT$12.93.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue NT$1.04 trillion (+28.1% QoQ, +105.6% YoY); gross profit NT$520.8 hundred-million, GM 5.02%; operating profit NT$342 hundred-million; net profit NT$286.5 hundred-million; EPS NT$7.43; TTM ROE above 40%; H1 revenue NT$1 trillion8458 hundred-million (+86.5% YoY), H1 EPS NT$12.93

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 AI server revenue is expected to grow QoQ but at a slower rate than Q2 off the high base; the full-year target of AI server revenue doubling YoY and general servers growing double-digit is unchanged, as is the target of AI reaching 80% of total server revenue in 2026 (75% to 80% in each of the first two quarters, servers over 80% of company revenue since Q1). Notebooks: Q3 shipments guided down roughly 20% QoQ and full-year shipments down double-digit YoY as memory and CPU price hikes and shortages bite; full-year overall margins expected to hold around H1 levels. From Q3, with some customers' agreement, part of the high-value component transactions on individual AI server projects shift from a buy-and-sell to a consignment model, changing revenue recognition, easing working-capital needs and reducing the gross-margin dilution from high-priced servers.
quarterly_data.figure: full-year AI server revenue to double YoY; AI 75% to 80% of server revenue, 80% full-year target unchanged; Q3 notebooks down about two-tenths QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: AI server rack ASP was roughly flat QoQ, showing the old-to-new generation transition has completed its handover; the big revenue jump came from strong volume growth while gross margin held steady, with the dilution from high-priced racks absorbed by product-mix optimisation after the sharp ASP jump in Q1. Beyond the top-5 cloud service providers (still the main AI revenue contributors), GPU AI servers for neocloud customers and ASIC AI server projects for large CSPs are both shipping in small volumes, progress in customer diversification.

Customer AI product planning and order visibility now extends to 2028, and existing capacity is insufficient, so the board approved acquiring AUO's Huaya plant in Guishan, Taoyuan for NT$19.7B - a former panel fab with high power capacity, next to Quanta's R&D headquarters and existing Taiwan server plants - mainly to serve 2028 orders (handover expected Q4 2027, payment mainly in 2027). With the new plant, Taiwan back-end AI server assembly capacity in 2028 is expected to double from today. The board also approved about US$1B of capital injections into overseas subsidiaries: US$973M into US subsidiary QMN for California AI server assembly/test capacity (power and infrastructure build-out plus equipment) and EUR19.5M into German subsidiary QCG for smart-cockpit automotive lines. AI server order visibility of over one year is normal for this ODM-direct, build-to-order B2B business.
quarterly_data.figure: AUO Huaya plant acquisition NT$197 hundred-million; order visibility to 2028; capital increases about US$10 hundred-million total - US$9.73 hundred-million to US QMN and EUR1950 ten-thousand to German QCG; 2028 Taiwan back-end AI assembly capacity to double

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 capex was NT$13.6B (H1 cumulative NT$21.8B), of which the California and Thailand sites together took over 80%; the plan to double AI production capacity by year-end versus end-2025 is on track. Based on the new plant plans, 2026 capex guidance was raised from NT$30B to NT$40B, all driven by strong, clearly visible customer demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capex NT$136 hundred-million; H1 capex NT$218 hundred-million; 2026 capex raised from NT$300 hundred-million to NT$400 hundred-million; AI capacity to double vs end-2025 by year-end

quarterly_data.signal: Notebook shipments were 11.5M units, up 15% QoQ (well above the flat-to-slightly-up guide) but down 5% YoY, as brand customers pulled orders forward on expectations that notebook memory supply will keep being crowded out by AI server memory demand and that memory prices keep rising; notebook gross margin stayed suppressed by memory and CPU shortages and price hikes. Chromebooks face the most severe component shortage and unfavourable supply terms because of their low ASP, staying below 10% of notebook shipments even in the seasonal education peak; brand customers are raising retail prices, further weakening demand, so H2 shipments will be below H1.
quarterly_data.figure: notebook shipments 1,150 ten-thousand units (+15% QoQ, -5% YoY); Chromebook below one-tenth of notebook shipments

quarterly_data.signal: AI servers contributed 75% to 80% of total server revenue in each of the first two quarters, with servers stably above 80% of company revenue since Q1 and notebooks contributing only a low-teens percentage; both AI and general-purpose servers grew strongly double-digit QoQ. AI server rack ASP was roughly flat QoQ, evidence that the generation handover has transitioned smoothly, and management maintains the 2026 target of AI reaching 80% of server revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: AI 75% to 80% of server revenue; servers above 80% of total revenue
